conviction_note: Several small sourced items that roughly cancel. NII tailwinds: Q2 NIM was up 11bp on securities reinvestment, Q3 has one more day than Q2 and rates rose through the quarter. Fee-line headwinds: the company guided deposit-fee cuts starting Q3, and the MBA series shows mortgage rates up about 65bp with refis down 56% y/y. A credit watch item (classified loans doubled in Q2) adds to the downside. impact_sum is -0.30 and the scaled number (p_up 49 x abs 2.8) is -0.06; both are near zero, which is the honest read on a one-to-two-estimate bank with no option chain.
bar: Q3 2026 diluted EPS $0.95 and revenue $65.2M (Earnings Whispers, https://beta.earningswhispers.com/go/w/CCBG, read 2026-10-19). A Benzinga search snippet gives $0.94 / $65.0M (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/CCBG/earnings-forecasts; page 403 on fetch, snippet only). Two sources agree within a penny. The bar is flat on Q2's $0.95 actual, which beat $0.90. The sweep reports n_estimates 1 and MarketBeat lists 4 ratings, so coverage is thin. The company gives no EPS guide; its only forward items are a ~23.5% FY26 tax rate and lower deposit fees from Q3.
positioning_check: Short interest 567,864 shares, 4.14% of float, 6.6 days to cover at the 2026-09-30 settlement, down 5.96% from 603,877 (MarketBeat, https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NASDAQ/CCBG/short-interest, read 2026-10-19). That is elevated against 0.76% / 2.3 days in Sept 2025 but not crowded. No skew: the option chain is empty (baseline options.status empty_chain). Tape: spot 49.14, 20d -2.09%, 5d +1.55%, 7% below the $53.60 52w high set early Aug 2026. Earnings Whispers shows the stock -3.4% since the July 21 beat and below its earnings-AVWAP of $50.58. KBW is market perform with a $54 PT (2026-07-22).

findings.finding: Mortgage rates rose through Q3 2026, from 6.65% (week to July 10) to 7.30% (week to Sept 25, the sixth straight weekly rise). In that last week refinance applications were -56% y/y and the unadjusted purchase index -14% y/y. That points to lower Q3 mortgage banking revenue at Capital City Home Loans than Q2's $4.66M (about 7% of revenue). Regions, a Southeast direct peer, reported 3Q26 mortgage income only -3% QoQ, so the hit is probably a few hundred thousand dollars, roughly -$0.01 to -$0.02 EPS.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 mortgage revenue was +$0.4M QoQ and was cited as the main noninterest income driver of a $0.05 beat; the stock rose +3.81%. No isolated reaction to a mortgage-only surprise is available.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus is flat at $0.95 on Q2's $0.95, which included the mortgage uplift. If a mortgage drop were in the estimate, the bar would sit below Q2. With 1-2 estimates, nobody models this line.
findings.independence: MBA's own July 15 release had the 30y at 6.65%, the highest since Aug 2025 (https://www.mba.org/news-and-research/newsroom/news/2026/07/15/mortgage-applications-decrease-in-latest-mba-weekly-survey). Against it, Regions mortgage income was only -3% QoQ (https://finviz.com/news/403470/regions-reports-earnings-of-611-million-and-eps-of-071-in-3q-2026). This is a proxy; CCBG has not confirmed it.

findings.finding: NII should keep growing in Q3. Q2 NIM rose 11bp to 4.35% on higher yields from new securities purchases and a 6bp fall in cost of funds. Q3 has 92 days against Q2's 91. Rates rose through the quarter: the FOMC hiked 25bp to 3.75-4.00% on 2026-09-16 and long rates climbed. Southeast peer Regions reported 3Q26 NII +1.6% QoQ and NIM +2bp. Each 1% of NII (~$0.44M) is about $0.02 EPS for CCBG.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 NIM +11bp with a $0.05 EPS beat bought +3.81%. Q4 2025 EPS of $0.80 missed $0.89 and the stock fell -5.17%. The stock has paid for NII/EPS surprises in both directions.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus $0.95 is flat QoQ, so it builds in no NII growth, or assumes the fee headwind fully offsets it. If the market expected margin expansion to continue, the bar would sit above Q2's actual.
findings.independence: FOMC statement 2026-09-16 (https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevents/pressreleases/monetary20260916a.htm) and Regions 3Q26 (https://finviz.com/news/403470/regions-reports-earnings-of-611-million-and-eps-of-071-in-3q-2026). Against: peers INDB (+6bp) and FBK (+7bp) reported higher deposit costs (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000776901/000077690126000152/exhibit991-indb09x30x2026e.htm). The hike came late in the quarter, so most of its effect falls in Q4.

findings.finding: In the Q2 release, management said a review of deposit products against peer practice will lead to changes that reduce fee revenue starting Q3 2026. Q2 deposit fees were $5.66M. The size of the reduction was not given.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior print isolates deposit fees. The stock rose +3.81% on the release that announced the change, so the market did not punish the warning.
findings.why_not_priced: The direction is inside what the company guided, so it is mostly priced. The open question is size: no number was given, so a cut larger than ~$0.5M a quarter would be news.
findings.independence: Same document as the NII finding (Q2 release), a different line. Quartr and 24/7 Wall St summaries repeat it (https://247wallst.com/cards/capital-city-bank-group-q2-2026-earnings-ccbg-01ky2nqx84wqtfvvbhsf0bg9gy). No independent quantification.

findings.finding: Credit watch item: in Q2, classified loans rose $15.3M to $29.8M on downgrades of four CRE relationships (two private schools, a hotel, a funeral home). NPAs rose to $13.4M (0.30% of assets) and annualised net charge-offs to 14bp from 10bp. Q3 risks higher provision or NPAs if any of these migrate.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q4 2025 miss ($0.80 vs $0.89) fell -5.17%. Credit is a known swing for EPS at this size: a $1M provision is about $0.045 EPS.
findings.why_not_priced: The flat $0.95 bar implies provision stays near Q2's $0.9M. A bar that priced migration would sit lower.
findings.independence: Same Q2 release as findings 2 and 3, a different line. No independent Q3 data on these specific credits; nothing dated after July speaks to them.

findings.finding: Short interest is 4.14% of float, 6.6 days to cover (567,864 shares at 2026-09-30, down 6% from the prior settlement). That is well above the 0.76% / 2.3 days of Sept 2025. On a ~78k-share/day name this is a modest squeeze cushion on an in-line or better print.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior print with comparable short interest observed.
findings.why_not_priced: It is a public number. The point is only that the short is not crowded enough to drive the reaction alone, and it leans against a negative.

findings.finding: Long rates rose through Q3 (mortgage rates +65bp, the Fed hiked in September), so AOCI on the AFS portfolio likely marked down. Tangible book per share ($28.07 at Q2, +2.0% QoQ) could grow less or dip, which banks are often judged on.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No isolated TBV reaction in the baseline.
findings.why_not_priced: The market does not reconcile AOCI on a one-analyst bank before the print. Retained earnings (~$16M a quarter against ~$480M TCE) likely offsets most of it.
findings.independence: Mortgage-rate series in finding 1 (same rate move, different line). This is an inference; the size of the AFS book is not checked here.

baseline_tension: No skew to agree or disagree with. The findings net to roughly zero, consistent with a stock 3.4% below its post-Q2 level and 7% off its high with a flat consensus. Nothing cuts sharply against the tape.
lessons_applied: Rule 5 (narrow proxy vs broader series): mortgage-rate finding cut -0.4 -> -0.25, because direct Southeast peer Regions reported mortgage income only -3% QoQ.
Rule 6 (inside guided range): deposit-fee finding moved toward 0, -0.2 -> -0.15; the direction was guided by the company.
Rule 7 / positioning: short interest not crowded, so the positioning finding was trimmed +0.2 -> +0.1. Rule 5 (inference) trimmed the AOCI/TBV inference -0.2 -> -0.1.
Pessimism artefact: the set leaned mildly negative on mostly proxies, so p_up was moved 48 -> 49; abs_move_pct kept at 2.8 (above the 2.02 median, per rule 8 / understatement).
Bar verified with two agreeing sources ($0.95 EW, $0.94 Benzinga), so no cap was applied. The NII and credit findings are left unchanged.
